text:
maria: Heads up — eu-west GPU nodepools are hitting hard capacity and we're seeing a spike of Pending inference pods with reason: Insufficient GPUs. Prod dedicated customers noticing tail latency increases. /cc @chris @noah
chris: seeing it in the dashboard (region:europe-west1). GCE quota appears fine, it's actual spare GPUs in the zone that are exhausted. A few AZs report preemptible losses earlier today.
noah: is this primarily preemptible-based warmpool churn? If so we can failover to reserved pools in the short term. Any impacted nodegroups listed?
maria: affected nodegroups: gpu-highmem-eu-a, gpu-highmem-eu-b. Warmpool scaling didn't attach fast enough. Some pods are nodeSelector: gpu=highmem and have PDBs so drain is slow.
diana: quick mitigation idea: mark a secondary regional pool (gpu-reserve-eu) with label spillover=true and adjust CA priorities so it scales before we start cross-region routes. We should also ensure tolerations/taints for low-priority jobs only.
chris: agree. Proposed steps: 1) patch cluster-autoscaler config to prioritize "gpu-reserve-eu" via expander: least-waste or node-group weight. 2) apply taint: gpu=dense:NoSchedule on primary pools and add tolerations to dedicated customer workloads. 3) for low-priority jobs, switch to cpu-fallback service.
maria: quick CA config we can apply (will rollout as an emergency change):
```
--
-- cluster-autoscaler configmap (snippet)
scale-up: {
  expander: "priority",
  priorities: [
    { "nodeGroup": "gpu-reserve-eu", "weight": 100 },
    { "nodeGroup": "gpu-highmem-eu-a", "weight": 50 }
  ]
}
--
```
noah: that priority expander snippet looks good but remember our CA build expects annotation based weights. I'll translate and push. Also we should increase maxNodes for gpu-reserve-eu temporarily to avoid scale-up throttling.
diana: I'll prepare the toleration/taint changes. For safety, we should exclude canary and latency-sensitive routes from being moved cross-region. We can use nodeAffinity + topologySpread to prefer same-zone.
maria: operational checklist before change: 1) add metric alert for cross-region egress cost increase, 2) add tracing tag so we can identify requests routed off-region, 3) notify support and tier-1.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-214580-3 — EU GPU pressure. Assignee: oncall. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-214580-3
chris: cost note — if we start new reserved capacity in us-west as last resort, egress will add ~1.5-2c/token for some customers. We should coordinate billing owners.
noah: also watch for NVLink topology differences across zones; larger models may fail placement if we move to single-GPU nodes. We'll add a validator to the scheduler (pod predicate) to prevent incompatible placements.
diana: rolling runbook (I'm going to paste commands):
```
# mark reserve pool scale-up
kubectl annotate configmap cluster-autoscaler configmap.kube-system "ca.priorities=gpu-reserve-eu:100,gpu-highmem-eu-a:50" --overwrite
# increase nodegroup max
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-reserve-eu --max-nodes=50 --region europe-west1
# taint primary poolskubectl taint nodes -l nodepool=gpu-highmem-eu-a gpu=dense:NoSchedule- || true
```
maria: ETA for the change? We need reduced Pending within 10m. If not, we escalate to cross-region spill.
chris: I'll push the CA annotation in 2m and monitor.
noah: I'll add the scheduler predicate and a dry-run admission check for the largest models.
diana: notifying support now, posting to #support-prod and tagging customers that might be affected. :loud_sound:
ops-bot: Update: CA annotation applied by chris at 2145801259.
maria: Observability — Pending queue dropped by ~60% after reserve pool scaled. Still seeing a few stragglers pinned by PDBs. If those don't reduce in 8m we do controlled cross-region spill to us-west.
chris: next steps if needed: 1) enable cross-region routing in the regional-router service, 2) scale down cpu-fallbacks in eu and scale up us-west reserved nodes, 3) add egress alert. Preparing scripts now.
noah: note for postmortem: track warmpool attach latency and improve attach logic so we don't need manual intervention next time. Also consider pre-warming MIG configurations for multi-instance models.
maria: thanks all. Keep updates here. If anyone finds a quick pattern in logs showing a single misbehaving deployment, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
